reuse.why: Factors the range rule into getRangeAmount and uses it inside getScheduledAmount, but the touched server sites keep their own missing/number/range dispatch instead of calling the existing getScheduledAmount, which already decides all three cases.

duplication.why: The range rule now exists once, yet the `null ? 0 : number ? v : range` dispatch remains copied at four sites (schedules/app.ts twice, forecast-schedules, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions) plus schedule-template's own variant.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getScheduledAmount, where schedule amount logic belongs.

scope.why: Only the ranged-amount computations, a test and a release note change.

maintainability.why: A future change to the range rule is a one-line edit, though the redundant per-site dispatch next to an equivalent helper invites drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts updateActions and postTransactionForSchedule, server/forecast/forecast-schedules.ts normalizeSchedule and shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions call getRangeAmount inside their own dispatch rather than the existing getScheduledAmount

one_place.where: getRangeAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts, used by getScheduledAmount and by every server-side ranged-amount site
